video.title: AI Agents Are Finally Easy to Set Up

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates setting up an OpenClaw agent on Hostinger to search for trending business stories and return summaries and content angles through Telegram. He adjusts the agent’s skills after web search fails, then suggests adding past episode transcripts and connecting tools for ongoing alerts. The video also mentions using timely trend coverage to attract views and starting an AI implementation agency for small businesses. The main takeaway is that a hosted agent can reduce setup friction, but its research still needs refinement and human review.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; demonstrates the setup and pitches possible uses.

ideas.name: Hosted AI trend research assistant
ideas.one_liner: A hosted AI agent searches for trending business topics and returns summaries and content angles to a creator.
ideas.business_model: Personal research automation for a podcast; an external revenue model is not stated.
ideas.customer: Koerner uses it for his podcast; broader customer types are not stated.
ideas.problem: Creators have limited time and find it hard to spot and cover a trend before others do.
ideas.offer: An OpenClaw agent searches the web for three trending ideas and stories, writes one-sentence summaries, and suggests a content angle. The owner can prompt it through Telegram or the Hostinger interface.

pricing.model: Not stated for an external product or service.
pricing.notes: The Hostinger plan price is not stated. The video says there is no per-agent fee and mentions an optional $6 API-key add-on.

ideas.delivery: OpenClaw runs on a managed Hostinger server, uses web search skills, and returns results in its chat interface, which Koerner accesses through Telegram or Hostinger. The agent performs the search and drafts the output; a human configures it, checks the results, and decides what to publish.
unit_economics_claims: Hostinger is described as charging no per-agent fee; the plan price is not stated.
An optional API-key setup add-on is described as costing $6.
The agent is said to run 24/7 on the hosted server.
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated overall. Hostinger plan price is not stated; an optional ready-to-use API-key add-on is stated as $6. The speaker contrasts this with a $700 Mac mini, plus unpriced peripherals.

acquisition.how: No customer acquisition process is shown. The agent automates research for its owner, but finding external paying customers would require a separate process.

onboarding.how: Managed OpenClaw reduces server setup, but the user still selects a model, supplies an API key, creates a Telegram bot, and approves the connection.

delivery.how: The agent searches and drafts results on demand and can run continuously. The demo required skill changes after search failed, and a human should review its output.

billing.how: No customer billing or payment process is described.

support.how: Software can handle the research task, but the demonstration required a person to troubleshoot search and change skills.

uk_applicability.notes: The workflow is online and has no stated US-only dependency. If the agent is extended to send marketing messages to UK individuals or sole traders, PECR consent rules apply; the transcript only demonstrates messaging the owner.

risks: Web search initially failed and required installing different skills.
The speaker says the first output was not much better than a Google or Reddit search.
Search results and generated summaries may be weak or inaccurate, so a person should verify claims before publishing.
The suggested integrations could expose inbox or messaging data; access should be limited to what the task needs.

tactics.name: Set up a managed OpenClaw server and Telegram bot
steps: Choose Managed OpenClaw on Hostinger and enable Instant Web Search.
Connect an Anthropic API key, or consider the optional ready-to-use key add-on described in the video.
Choose Telegram, create a bot through BotFather, paste its token into the setup, and approve the matching connection code.
Test the agent by asking it to research a topic.

quote.text: I'm gonna choose Telegram because I already use it for other stuff. Okay, you can use Telegram on your desktop or on your phone.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use a specific research prompt
steps: Define the agent as a trend research assistant for approachable small-business ideas.
Ask it to search the web for the top three trending ideas and stories.
Request one-sentence summaries, one content angle, and a clean numbered list.
Tailor the prompt to the subject area; the host suggests adding home-service ideas.

quote.text: When I ask for ideas, search the web for the top three trending novel and approachable business ideas and stories of people that are building cool products or services for each topic right a one sentence summary and suggest one content angle I can post about today send it as a clean numbered list.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Troubleshoot web search by changing skills
steps: When the initial web search fails, open the skills area.
Search ClawHub for web_search and web_fetch and install them.
Turn off browser automation, return to chat, and retry the prompt.

quote.text: I'm gonna search under claw hub, web underscore search, and then I'm gonna install that, okay? This will just make this work more cleanly than that, and then I'm also gonna search web underscore fetch.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Personalize the agent to the creator
steps: Upload transcripts from earlier episodes so the agent can learn the creator's preferred words and vocal patterns.

quote.text: I would train this agent on my content, on my voice. I would upload transcripts from previous episodes so it knows what words I like to say, how I talk my vocal patterns, et cetera.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Turn on proactive trend alerts
steps: Connect the agent to other tools such as Zapier or Gmail.
Use Twilio if the preferred alert is a text or call.
Set the agent to notify the owner when a relevant business idea or story appears.

quote.text: So it could text me or call me or whatever I prefer any time, a new, crazy, incredible business idea or story drops that might be relevant to the type of content I post about.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Choose a model for cost and capability
steps: Check which model the installation selected by default.
Compare the default Haiku model with a more capable model for the intended task.
Account for API-key costs; the video does not state model usage prices.

quote.text: It's using haiku, which is a fairly cheap and somewhat old, at least the AR world is kind of old. Claude or anthropic model, I would prefer it uses Opus 4.7, which is the newest and pretty incredible.
